messages.subject: Canopy and Dirichlet
parts:
Hi Yuchao,

I have 3 question on Canopy which I am testing for my clonal evolution study:

  1. Is Dirichlet process used to define optimal # of clones? If not, could it be implemented?
  2. When running more then 100 variants (sna only mode) Canopy seems to have trouble to pass post step with cutoff = 0.05 and if I run longer (as suggested) it produces an error (subscript ouf of bounds, post not found etc). So is there a sweet spot on how many chains, burning, writeskip parameters to be used to produce meaningful results that would pass 0.05 cutoff?
  3. How about sex chromosome variants. So if my SNA is on X chromosome and it is a male patient sample, should I specify it in CNA matrix since it would be like a "CNA" in a sense? SNA only mode only takes R and X and  Canopy is unaware of variants locations in this case.

Thank you

Best,

Chingiz

NIH

messages.subject: Re: [canopy_phylogeny] Canopy and Dirichlet
parts:
Hi Chingiz,

I’m very sorry for my late reply — I just graduated and things are crazy. Please see my answers below.
1. Is Dirichlet process used to define optimal # of clones? If not, could it be implemented?
We use BIC to determine the number of clones.

1. When running more then 100 variants (sna only mode) Canopy seems to have trouble to pass post step with cutoff = 0.05 and if I run longer (as suggested) it produces an error (subscript ouf of bounds, post not found etc). So is there a sweet spot on how many chains, burning, writeskip parameters to be used to produce meaningful results that would pass 0.05 cutoff?

It can be hard to determine whether the chain has converged or not, although it doesn’t make sense for the error that you encountered. Can you send me the image file of the 100 variants (use save.image() function) as well as the script that you use for Canopy?

The number of chains should be as large as possible. However this also depends on the computation power and the complexity of the problem (i.e., if there is only one posterior mode and each chain converges very easily to the mode, there is no need to run many chains). The burnin should be set with regard to the posterior likelihood plot that is generated by Canopy. However, since there is a writeskip step where we only store every k^th posterior tree, this value usually doesn’t have to be too large.

1. How about sex chromosome variants. So if my SNA is on X chromosome and it is a male patient sample, should I specify it in CNA matrix since it would be like a "CNA" in a sense? SNA only mode only takes R and X and  Canopy is unaware of variants locations in this case.

SNVs and CNAs from sex chromosome are not currently enabled by Canopy. It needs special attention (between males and females and X chr and Y chr) and is not currently not implemented.

Hope that this is of help to you,
Yuchao
